description: Prompts for running structured due diligence before making an offer or exchanging contracts.

cards.title: Due Diligence Risk Scan
cards.description: The questions you need answered before you sign anything.
cards.prompt:
You are an Australian property due diligence analyst. I want to run a structured risk scan on a property before I make an offer or exchange contracts.

PROPERTY: [address / suburb, state, type]
AGE: [approximate build year]
STRATA: [yes / no / unknown]
CONTRACT / SECTION 32: [available / not yet]
PRICE: $[amount]
KNOWN ISSUES: [anything flagged already, or 'none']

Please return:
1. Contract and title flags (questions for my solicitor)
2. Building and pest flags (questions for my inspector)
3. Strata / body corporate flags (if applicable)
4. Suburb and zoning flags (check with council)
5. Finance flags (check with my broker)
6. Red flags summary table
7. Pre-exchange due diligence checklist

DISCLAIMER: General information and preparation only. Not legal, financial, or building advice. Do not exchange contracts without independent legal advice from a solicitor or conveyancer.
cards.best_for: Buyers and investors who have a property in mind and want to run a structured pre-offer risk check
cards.professional_review_note: Contract review requires a qualified solicitor or conveyancer. Building and pest requires an on-site inspector. Finance flags require a licensed mortgage broker.

cards.title: Strata Document Review Prep
cards.description: Prepare the right questions to ask when reviewing a strata report.
cards.prompt:
You are an Australian property analyst helping me prepare to review a strata or body corporate report. The property is [type, beds, baths] in [suburb, state]. The building has approximately [X] units/lots.

Please help me understand what to look for and ask about:
1. Sinking fund — what is a healthy balance for a building this size and age?
2. Special levies — what triggers them and how do I spot the risk?
3. Building defect claims — what to look for in minutes and reports
4. Body corporate insurance — what does it cover and what gaps do I need to insure for?
5. Bylaws — what restrictions most affect investors or owner-occupiers?
6. 8 specific questions to ask my solicitor or strata specialist

DISCLAIMER: General education and preparation only. Not legal advice. Strata document review requires a qualified solicitor or strata specialist.
cards.best_for: Buyers considering apartments, townhouses, or any strata-titled property
cards.output_type: Strata due diligence guide and question list
cards.professional_review_note: Always have a qualified solicitor or strata specialist review strata documents before exchanging contracts.
